description.narrative:
Insatsen avser ett kärnstöd till organisationen Front Line Defenders under perioden 2020-2022. För denna period ska Front Line Defenders genomföra sin strategiska plan med fokus på följande områden:
1)Ge snabbt, flexibelt och effektivt 24-timmars akut- och nödstöd i relation till skyddsbehoven hos utsatta mänskliga rättighetsförsvarare. 2)Stärka mänskliga rättighetsförsvarares motståndskraft och kapacitet att hantera sin säkerhet och sitt skydd. 3)Förbättra synligheten för mänskliga rättighetsförsvarare och de positiva effekterna av deras arbete. 4)Stärka det nationella, regionala och internationella skyddet av utsatta människorättsförsvarare.

2023 in a snapshot/Summary:
• Front Line Defenders (FLD) supported 2,413 Human Rights Defenders (HRDs) at risk and 647 organisations, communities and collectives in 130 countries. 83% of HRDs were able to continue their human rights work following the receipt of FLD support. This included 80% of men HRDs, 83% of women HRDs (WHRDs), and 89% of gender nonconforming HRDs. 99% of organisations, communities and collectives FLD worked with were able to continue their work, demonstrating the additional resilience that groups have in the face of threats. The overall figure of 83% is higher than in 2022 (77%), largely as a result of providing grants to fewer HRDs from Afghanistan compared to 2022, when many Afghan HRDs had to stop their work immediately after the Taliban takeover, impacting global results. • FLD provided grants to HRDs amounting to €3,297,378 including 1,248 protection grants to 930 individuals and 306 organisations at risk in 98 countries. • FLD's protection coordination team provided 1,246 consultations to HRDs at risk. • 342 HRDs participated in workshops/consultations focused on risk analysis and protection planning and wellbeing. • 308 HRDs and 193 human rights organisations in 76 countries were supported by Digital Protection Consultants, and 543 HRDs were supported by FLD Security Advisor. • FLD published its annual Global Analysis research presenting trends, key issues and important developments related to human rights defenders work and security around the world including the only annual documentation of all HRDs killed each year. • The 2023 Front Line Defenders Award was presented to five winners.
The organisation continued to review and monitor impact and performance in accordance with the Monitoring & Evaluation Plan and the Results Framework. Some highlights from 2023 included: • 99% of HRDs reported improved security as a result of a grant. • 50% of respondents said the grant made not only the HRD secure, but also their colleagues and/or family. • 96% of HRDs reported using digital security tools as a result of received advice.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
